EKF Residual-Enhanced CNN–BiLSTM for Explainable GNSS Spoofing and Jamming Detection¶

Thesis experiment notebook — reproducible, source-group-disjoint, and cost-sensitive

tl;dr¶

On the final held-out source groups, the proposed CNN–BiLSTM with EKF residuals achieved 91.0% accuracy, 0.867 macro-F1, and 0.856 macro recall. Per-class recall was 98.8% Normal, 58.9% Spoofing, and 99.3% Jamming.

The controlled EKF ablation is substantial: removing EKF features reduced accuracy from 91.0% to 57.0% and macro-F1 from 0.867 to 0.618. Random Forest remains the strongest aggregate model in this Kaggle-conditioned semi-synthetic experiment (97.4% accuracy), so the deep model is not presented as universally superior.

The principal unresolved weakness is stealthy gradual drift: proposed-model recall is 34.6%, compared with 73.8% for sudden spoofing jumps. Results describe controlled injected attacks and do not establish field performance. Across five neural training seeds, the proposed model achieved 0.857 mean macro-F1 (SD 0.034).

Context & methods¶

Research question¶

Does adding EKF innovation/residual information improve balanced three-class detection relative to an otherwise identical CNN–BiLSTM that receives only navigation/IMU features?

Evaluation safeguards¶

  • The unit of independence is a Kaggle source segment. Its matched Normal, Spoofing, and Jamming variants are kept together in exactly one split.
  • Scaling is fit on training groups only. Early stopping and class-decision costs use validation groups only.
  • The test set is held out until final evaluation; overlapping windows are never treated as independent for confidence intervals.
  • The primary selection criteria are macro-F1, macro recall, and attack-class recall—not accuracy alone.
  • Source groups are assigned approximately 70/15/15 to train/validation/test.
  • The experiment uses five neural training seeds for the primary EKF ablation.

Key assumptions¶

The supplied Kaggle rows are used directly as the source of ordered speed, IMU, gyro, and altitude patterns. Because their consecutive latitude/longitude fixes are not physically coherent, those patterns condition a local kinematic carrier rather than being treated as an unmodified flight path. Synthetic attacks are then inserted into the GNSS channel of each Kaggle-derived carrier. The result is explicitly semi-synthetic, not field attack data.

Interpretation. The file is complete and timestamps are unique, but its median implied horizontal GNSS speed is about 1,017 m/s while its recorded median speed is about 17.7 m/s; 99.3% of successive fixes imply more than 100 m/s. IMU, speed, and position therefore do not form one plausible flight trajectory. Applying an EKF directly to these rows makes normal innovations attack-like and removes the physical basis for the proposed method.

The defensible remedy is a transparent carrier transformation: consecutive 100-row Kaggle segments supply speed and sensor variation, a bounded kinematic reconstruction restores physical continuity, and attack effects are then inserted into GNSS only. Source row ranges are retained for provenance; raw-coordinate performance is not claimed.

3. Build Kaggle-conditioned carriers and inject attacks¶

Each non-overlapping Kaggle segment produces matched Normal, Spoofing, and Jamming variants. Recorded speed and robust IMU/gyro patterns condition the carrier motion. Spoofing comprises gradual coordinate dragging and sudden jumps. Jamming comprises high-variance measurement corruption and signal freezing. Attack onset, direction, magnitude, and noise are randomized per flight. An attack persists to flight end; otherwise the abrupt return to clean GNSS would create an unlabeled recovery anomaly.

4. EKF innovation/residual generation¶

The implemented estimator is a genuine EKF. Its state is north/east/up position, horizontal speed, heading, and vertical speed. The coordinated-motion prediction is nonlinear because position depends on $v\cos\psi$ and $v\sin\psi$; covariance propagation uses the analytical state Jacobian. GNSS position and reported speed form a four-dimensional measurement. Innovation is recorded before the gated update. A finite-difference test verifies the analytical process Jacobian to within $10^{-5}$.

This robust gate is part of the estimator design and is disclosed because it materially affects separability. It must be re-calibrated for a real vehicle and receiver.

Results¶

6. Train baselines and the controlled EKF ablation¶

Random Forest and SVM use mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, last value, and linear slope for every window feature. CNN-only, LSTM-only, and both CNN–BiLSTM variants use full sequences. The two CNN–BiLSTM variants have the same architecture and training procedure; only the EKF feature group differs. Deep models use focal loss, moderate class weighting, early stopping on validation macro-F1, and no test feedback.

In [7]:
classical_models = gp.train_classical_models(full, cfg.seed)
neural_specs = {
    "CNN-only": (gp.CNNClassifier(len(full_features), cfg.dropout), full),
    "LSTM-only": (gp.LSTMClassifier(len(full_features), cfg.dropout), full),
    "CNN-BiLSTM without EKF": (gp.CNNBiLSTMClassifier(len(gp.BASE_FEATURES), cfg.dropout), base),
    "CNN-BiLSTM with EKF": (gp.CNNBiLSTMClassifier(len(full_features), cfg.dropout), full),
}
trained_models, history_frames = {}, []
for name, (model, windows) in neural_specs.items():
    model, history = gp.train_torch_model(model, windows, cfg, device, name)
    trained_models[name] = (model, windows)
    history_frames.append(history)
    print(f"{name}: {len(history)} epochs; best val macro-F1={history.val_macro_f1.max():.3f}")
training_history = pd.concat(history_frames, ignore_index=True)
gp.save_table(training_history, paths["tables"] / "training_history.csv")

7. Validation-only decision tuning and final test evaluation¶

Because missing attacks is costlier than a modest false-alarm increase, class-probability biases are selected on validation groups using a predeclared composite of macro-F1, macro recall, mean attack recall, and minimum class recall. This changes only the decision rule, not model weights. Final uncertainty uses a cluster bootstrap over complete Kaggle source groups; each resampled group includes its matched Normal, Spoofing, and Jamming variants.

In [9]:
threshold_cfg = gp.tune_ekf_threshold(raw_full, full_features)
metrics, per_class, probabilities, predictions, class_biases = gp.evaluate_models(
    classical_models, trained_models, raw_full, full_features, threshold_cfg, device
)
test_y = raw_full["test"]["y"]
test_flights = raw_full["test"]["flight_id"]
test_source_groups = raw_full["test"]["source_segment_id"]

    f1_lo, f1_hi = gp.flight_bootstrap_ci(test_y, pred, test_source_groups, "macro_f1", seed=cfg.seed)

9. Five-seed EKF ablation robustness¶

The full experiment runner repeats the matched with-EKF and without-EKF networks for seeds 42, 52, 62, 72, and 82 on the fixed source-group split. This isolates optimisation-seed sensitivity; it does not substitute for evaluation over alternative data partitions.

ROC–AUC is reported as a ranking diagnostic, not the primary endpoint: the operational question is multiclass assignment under unequal error costs, and class distributions are not the only concern. Macro-F1, macro recall, the confusion matrix, and per-class recall therefore carry more weight in interpretation.

Two complementary validation-only explanations are reported. Sequence permutation measures the change in macro-F1 after moving a complete feature trajectory between windows, whereas GradientSHAP attributes model logits relative to a training-window background. Agreement supports robustness; disagreement is expected for correlated residual channels. Neither is a causal explanation. Latency is batch-one framework latency on the recorded device and excludes sensor acquisition, window accumulation, preprocessing, and EKF computation.

Takeaways¶

  1. The Kaggle data now participate in model construction. Non-overlapping source segments provide speed and sensor patterns, while an explicit kinematic transformation repairs coordinate continuity before controlled attack insertion.
  2. EKF residuals materially improve balanced performance. Relative to the controlled CNN–BiLSTM ablation, the proposed model improves accuracy by 34.0% points, macro-F1 by 0.248, and macro recall by 0.221.
  3. The proposed model is useful but not universally best. Random Forest has the highest aggregate test score, while the proposed model provides a temporal architecture and a direct EKF ablation aligned with the thesis hypothesis.
  4. Spoofing remains the limiting class. The aggregate spoofing recall of 58.9% hides a major subtype gap: gradual drift remains difficult at 34.6%. Jamming is much more separable in this generator and should not be described as equally difficult.
  5. These are semi-synthetic results. A source-group split, five training seeds, and source-group bootstrap intervals limit common overstatement, but only real receiver logs, unseen trajectories, and hardware-in-the-loop attacks can establish external validity.

Limitations and threats to validity¶

  • Semi-synthetic-to-real gap: injected attacks cannot reproduce every receiver, multipath, satellite geometry, RF front-end, or adversary adaptation.
  • Source transformation: recorded sensor patterns are retained, but the carrier path is a bounded kinematic reconstruction rather than an unmodified recorded trajectory.
  • Estimator-assisted separability: the robust innovation gate is an explicit design choice and can amplify attack residuals. It requires calibration and sensitivity analysis on real data.
  • Gradual spoofing: slow, kinematically plausible coordinate dragging can remain close to the estimator trajectory. Additional receiver observables (C/N0, AGC, Doppler, satellite residuals, clock bias) are the most credible next features.
  • Uncertainty: confidence intervals are wide because the independent sample size is the seven held-out source groups, not the number of overlapping windows.
  • No deployment claim: latency excludes upstream sensing and preprocessing, and no safety assurance, adversarial robustness, or distribution-shift study was performed.
